wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: US forces struck Iran's Qeshm Island ahead of the midterm elections, the same day Tehran set five conditions for regional security, among them recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz. Afterwards Vance said Trump conceded the Iran war lost Congress, and Trump insisted only he decides when it ends.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: The war with Iran made the Strait of Hormuz a war zone: UK Maritime Trade Operations counted 11 attacks on shipping in the week to November 4, and a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire. Yet JP Morgan put October's surplus at 1.4 million barrels a day as high prices destroyed demand, and Pakistan cut fuel prices a fifth straight time.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The Iran war priced it through the Strait of Hormuz: mines and tanker fires held it up, and peace hopes after the midterms pulled it back. JP Morgan estimates a 1.4 million barrel-a-day surplus in October, and with freight to Asia at $30-$35 a barrel, Valero says, US Gulf Coast refiners are booking the gap as profit.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: Gas abroad tightened. Strikes cut Iran's gas capacity by a fifth, and European gas passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022. QatarEnergy then agreed to buy up to 3 million tonnes of US liquefied natural gas a year. That demand reaches American prices through the export terminals that ship it.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's news came after the latest reading and turned on Black Sea supply: Zelensky said Turkey will help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, Rubio saw growing interest in a ceasefire there, and a weak Russian export outlook lifted wheat again. Pakistan raised its support price to Rs4,500 a maund.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.
rice.recent: The fortnight's food news was about other things: Thai inflation breaching the central bank's ceiling at 3.9%, a flawed wheat policy behind a flour crisis and a new sowing target in Punjab, and climbing food prices in Honduras. None of it was about the rice trade.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Chinese buyers paid a record $200-plus a ton above London prices, a squeeze fed by AI demand, and the rally fattened earnings from Adani Enterprises to Mitsubishi Corporation. Since then copper has slipped to its lowest since July on fears the Democratic midterm sweep will slow the AI data-centre build-out it was counting on.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Higher yields mark down bonds banks already hold: Bank of America's unrealized losses on them rose to $109 billion. The Fed then left rates unchanged, and Warsh's muddled messaging revived doubts over its credibility; after the midterms Democrats took control of confirming every future Fed governor, and the dollar fell while gold jumped.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: The fall gathered after the midterms delivered a Democratic sweep. On Thursday Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11%, as a backlash against AI data centres met a Congress whose majority threatened the spending that fills chipmakers' order books. The rout then spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: Chipmakers led the slide after the midterms: on Thursday Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% as traders bet a Democratic Congress would slow the US data-centre spending those chips are sold into. Days earlier, Anthropic's prospectus showed it lost $80.7 billion on $16.3 billion of revenue, a hard look at what AI's builders earn.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The fortnight's fuel news was about diesel, not gasoline: Russia extended its diesel export ban through January, Ukraine's drones hit refineries at Kstovo and Ryazan after a mid-October pause, and the first Russian diesel tanker sailed for New York under Trump's deal with Putin to lower fuel prices. None of it names the US pump price.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The war with Iran is behind it: Hormuz is mined, Qatar's carrier Al Mayeda was struck in the Gulf, and strikes cut Iran's own gas capacity by a fifth, leaving Europe competing for scarcer LNG. The European price then passed €100 per megawatt hour, its highest since 2022, and Britain faced LNG at triple its pre-crisis cost.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.
vix.recent: Bitcoin fell to a seven-week low on the day of the high, and Paraguay's president Santiago Pena resigned after the closure of Ueno bank. Neither of those stories, nor Aramco's gains from the Hormuz crisis, accounts for the price options traders are paying for protection.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight's news on Pakistan's money was about what it owes: World Bank figures put its external debt at $135.1bn in 2025, nearly double a decade earlier, with China the biggest lender at $22.4 billion. Petrol and diesel were cut for a fifth straight time. None of it accounts for the rupee's small drift.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: Tinubu asked for $20.5 billion and €1.04 billion in foreign loans a week after launching his re-election bid, at a time when petrol cost about 1,400 naira a litre. Neither the borrowing request nor the campaign accounts for the naira's drift against the dollar over the window.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound's weakest day came just after parliament voted behind closed doors to defend Saudi Arabia, drawing Egypt into the Saudi-Houthi conflict. The recovery since ran alongside the Suez Canal's best month since 2023: $724 million in October, up 94% despite Houthi Red Sea threats, and canal tolls are paid in dollars.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's news from Turkey was diplomatic: Erdoğan backed restoring Ukraine's Black Sea grain corridor, and Turkey joined Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in demanding Hormuz reopen. None of it accounts for the lira's price.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: Garment workers demanded 30,000 taka a month, up from 12,500, and the government formed a wage board as protests disrupted factories for a third day. Nothing in the input connects those protests to the currency's price.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: Jakarta dismissed the president's chief of staff and detained three top police officers over alleged wiretapping of the president, with 20,980 troops deploying in the capital. Earlier, Indonesia cut gas supplies to Singapore, and October inflation eased to 3.23%. None of the reporting ties any of this to the rupiah.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: The fortnight's strain in Lebanon showed up in prices rather than in the exchange rate: Palestinian refugees in Beddawi, outside Tripoli, were squeezed by high energy prices and inflation, while Israeli forces bulldozed olive groves at Kfarshouba. None of it accounts for the pound's near-flat rate.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: Behind the firming sits a record trade surplus of $938.1 billion through September, and Beijing has started leaning against it: the PBOC tightened its forex reserve rules, a change worth up to $24 billion in foreign currency. Against the euro the yuan has gained 9%, and exporters in Ningbo are absorbing the squeeze.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The RBI stepped in with likely dollar sales that lifted the rupee to 95.02, defending a currency exposed to the oil bill. India is also cutting that exposure at the source: its crude now arrives from about 43 countries, spreading supply away from the Strait of Hormuz.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The real fell from the day Lula beat Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff, a sell-off billed as Brazil's Black Monday. Brazilian companies had already moved money into dollar stablecoins before the win. A week later, economists raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34%.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Pemex posted a $573 million loss even as oil prices surged, and Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas, who lost the fraud-marred 1988 election, died at 92. Neither accounts for the peso's move.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: Christine Lagarde said she would leave the European Central Bank in February, and the race to replace her narrowed to Klaas Knot, a hawk, and Pablo Hernández de Cos. Forecasters lifted euro zone inflation to 3.0% as European gas passed €100, but none of the reporting ties these to the exchange rate.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen's one rally came when the dollar fell on the US midterms and the yen gained 0.7%. Otherwise it stayed soft: foreign flows into US equities hit a record on the AI boom, and foreign issuers sold a record $16 billion of yen bonds to fund AI.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The firming ran through weeks of peace diplomacy: a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire in Oleshky, Nordic leaders' talks with Putin, then the first US-mediated talks with Ukraine since February, set for Abu Dhabi on 10 November. The Bank of Russia then raised its rate path, forecasting fourth-quarter inflation of 7.1-7.6%.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: The news of the period ran against a stronger rand. The US suspended South Africa from AGOA, the scheme that carried $1.7 billion of its duty-free exports in 2025. Local elections left 110 councils projected to hang as ActionSA took ANC township wards in Gauteng. None of it accounts for the firming.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: The $6.3 billion theft from Binance, which the FBI blamed on North Korea's TraderTraitor, drew a net $4.72 billion out of the exchange once withdrawals reopened. The CLARITY Act stalled 49 to 50 in the Senate, and an AI-led tech rout pulled about $430 million from US bitcoin ETFs as $1.26 billion in leveraged bets were liquidated.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: The fall ran through the $6.3 billion theft from Binance, which the FBI blamed on North Korea's TraderTraitor and tied to laundering through Ethereum. North Korea denied it, and Binance covered 90% of losses before resuming withdrawals. A week earlier the US Senate fell short of the 60 votes the Clarity Act needed, leaving the market's rules unwritten.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: The rebound came with the Democratic sweep in the US midterms, which pulled down the dollar and yields and sent money out of AI stocks into bullion, gold's biggest weekly gain since August. The pullback before it drew buyers: China extended its gold-buying streak to two years, and India's festive demand picked up.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Late October was about the bill for AI: Alphabet's capex jumped 114% in one quarter and its cash flow turned negative, Amazon's 12-month cash burn hit a record $42.4 billion, and Anthropic's IPO filing warned its AI could blackmail people. The selloff then reached Asia, where South Korea halted trading Friday after the Kospi fell 8%.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: The first US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks since February open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, with Europe left out, after a Melania Trump-brokered ceasefire let an aid convoy into Oleshky. In Moscow, Putin seized Japan Tobacco's Russian business, the maker of 37% of Russia's tobacco market.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: The peak followed US strikes on Qeshm Island and a Revolutionary Guards claim that 3 tankers hit mines in Hormuz, while Iran made recognition of its sovereignty over the strait a condition for a ceasefire. Since then 4 tankers have burned, a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire and 3 ships sank in 7 days.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: UK Maritime Trade Operations counted 11 attacks on commercial shipping in the seven days to November 4, eight of them in the strait, and three vessels sunk. Iran says tankers are burning after hitting mines, and a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire. Buyers are routing around it: India now takes crude from about 43 countries.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: With Hormuz mined, ships are returning to the Red Sea: the Suez Canal earned $724 million in October, its best month since the Houthi attacks began, with revenue up 94%. Late October's Houthi strikes hit Saudi Arabia and Aden, not shipping: a Saudi pipeline, a refinery claim that lifted Brent, and oil sites.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Egypt's canal earned $724 million in October, its highest monthly revenue since 2023 and up 94% despite Houthi Red Sea threats, as ships returned to the route. Late in October, Egypt's parliament authorised military support for Saudi Arabia, moving Cairo off the sidelines in the Saudi-Houthi conflict on the canal's southern approach.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Days after the trough, Taiwan's map showed 53 Chinese ships around the island, 34 of them warships. Nothing reported in the fortnight describes a closure, a declared drill zone or a rerouting that would account for the fall in transits, and the sea was calm.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: The danger sits on the Black Sea side: three drones hit the Contship Jet off Bulgaria and sank it, all 18 crew surviving, and Romania blamed Russia after a drone sank a ship. Erdoğan urged Russia and Ukraine to stop the attacks, Zelensky said Turkey will help restore Ukraine's grain corridor, and Rubio sees growing interest in a Black Sea ceasefire.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: The fortnight's news from around the strait was Spain's Toledo rail collision, which killed 68, and a US Treasury action against a Chandigarh couple faking Iranian tankers' flags. Neither accounts for the drop in traffic.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The news from France in these weeks was riots, more than 500 arrests, a national strike over wages and a Fitch outlook cut. None of it reached the ports or the shipping lanes, and none of it accounts for the fall in traffic through the strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: This fortnight's shipping news came from the Strait of Hormuz, not this route. Limpet mines and explosives disabled tankers there, and a seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire, all after the last reading on this chart. None of it accounts for traffic around the Cape.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touches the strait or the shipping through it. The war's news ran instead on the Oleshky ceasefire and the aid convoy that followed it, and on the US-mediated talks between Ukraine and Russia that open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The fortnight's Turkish news was diplomatic: Erdoğan pressed Russia and Ukraine to stop Black Sea attacks and backed restoring Ukraine's grain corridor, Turkey joined Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in demanding Hormuz reopen, and Aliyev skipped a Turkic summit. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Kuala Lumpur was political, not financial: Najib Razak left Kajang prison for house arrest after UMNO crowdfunded his fine, and Binance sought a return to Malaysia with a licence. Neither of these, nor the fiscal consolidation in Malaysia's 2027 Budget, accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Over the fortnight, Indonesia's president dismissed his chief of staff and police arrested three top police officers over alleged wiretapping, while Jakarta cut gas supplies to Singapore and October inflation eased to 3.23%. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Tech stocks drove the slide on AI worries, knocking 3% off the Nikkei on 30 October. A week later the AI rout spread across Asia, and South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. The same day Russia seized Japan Tobacco's local business, and BOJ chief Ueda saw upside risks to inflation.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Friday's fall came as a rout in AI shares spread across Asia, and South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. The rout reached a market whose heaviest names are China's AI builders. That same week Tencent expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold, and Alibaba's Qwen began running inside Siri.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: China's blue-chip index fell 11 weeks straight, a record, as AI stocks repriced: Contemporary Amperex's shares fell 15% despite 21.2 billion yuan quarterly profit. Results split the market, tech profit up 140% and property losing 53.2 billion yuan, while new export orders fell to 48.7 in October as a strong yuan squeezed exporters.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The slide came as a rout in AI stocks spread to Asia, and on Friday South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. The market's weight sits in Samsung and SK Hynix, whose AI-chip demand had also lifted the economy: South Korea grew 1% last quarter, 3x the forecast.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Mumbai's month belonged to Jio Platforms, whose record offer filled in 100 minutes and listed 25% above issue price at $137.1 billion. Alongside it came likely central-bank dollar sales to defend the rupee and carmakers' October dispatch of 525,000 cars. None of it explains the climb.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's fortnight was about energy. Indonesia cut the gas that generates up to 95% of the city's electricity, Saudi Arabia agreed to store crude in the Jurong caverns as mines filled Hormuz, and the USS Theodore Roosevelt called on its way to the Iran war. None of it was reported as moving the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The AI rout that spread across Asia on Friday reached Taipei, where TSMC carries about a third of the index; South Korea halted trading after the Kospi fell 8%. A day earlier, Micron paused work on a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant after about 12 workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Australia went into November set for a fifth rate hike as its inflation fight intensified, a decision awaited while oil prices slumped and Japan's Nikkei fell on AI worries. None of it accounts for the index's path over the window.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was its local elections, with 110 councils projected to hang and ActionSA taking township wards in Gauteng. The US also suspended its AGOA duty-free access, which carried $1.7 billion of exports in 2025. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: The slide followed Lula's runoff win over Flávio Bolsonaro, the market's pick: real futures fell 10% on what Bloomberg called Brazil's Black Monday, and companies moved cash into dollar stablecoins. Economists then raised their 2027 inflation forecast to 4.76% from 4.34% and lifted their rate forecasts with it.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was the death of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas at 92 and a $573 million loss at Pemex despite surging oil prices. Neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: The Argentine stories since then, a court dropping the $LIBRA probe into Milei and Chinese brands supplying 88.4% of Argentina's electric cars, all came after this series ends, and none of them explains the index.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada's news ran on trade and energy: Trump lifted some Canada tariffs, a Quebec paper mill idled most of its 360 workers, and a Conservative win in British Columbia boosted Mark Carney's energy ambitions. None of it is tied to a move in the energy, mining and bank shares that set this index.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The Democratic sweep in the midterms hit the chip makers hardest: amid a backlash against data centres, Nvidia fell 6%, AMD 12% and Micron 11% in one session. Doubts over AI spending deepened when OpenAI banked $11 billion of a round once planned at $30 billion.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The Bank of England raised rates on a forecast that inflation will peak at 4.9%, a day before an AI rout halted trading in South Korea after the Kospi fell 8%. Higher rates fed HSBC, whose quarterly pretax profit hit $9.6 billion, while JP Morgan's estimate of a 1.4 million barrel-a-day surplus weighed on oil.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight's German news ran on interest rates: Nagel of the Bundesbank backed a December move that would be the ECB's third hike this year, forecasters lifted euro zone inflation to 3.0%, and Lagarde quit early. Ifo expectations rose a sixth time and Schaeffler cut 3,500 jobs, but none of it accounts for a particular turn in the index.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: French shares fell alongside French government debt: long-term yields climbed from 4% in August to above 5%, and the state now borrows at higher rates than its own companies. The economy shrank 0.1% before Fitch cut France's outlook. Cost-of-living riots brought more than 500 arrests, and unions then called a national wage strike.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: ASML said customers are already asking for lithography tools for 2029 and 2030, as advanced packaging for AI chips soaks up supply. Against that, forecasters lifted euro zone inflation to 3.0%, and a French bond rout hung over the race between Knot and De Cos to replace Lagarde at the European Central Bank.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The fortnight's news from Spain was a rail collision near Toledo that killed at least 68 people, a data breach at the supplier Amadeus that exposed passengers of six Asian airlines, and Leapmotor building cars in Zaragoza. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's main banking story was the ECB clearing Intesa Sanpaolo to bid €32 billion for Monte dei Paschi. ECB policymakers also brought a rate hike debate into the open, which matters to a market this heavy in banks. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The franc rose almost 1% as the US midterms weakened the dollar, Swiss inflation accelerated to its highest in almost three years, and the SNB reported a nine-month profit on foreign currencies and gold. None of it accounts for the index's own path.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The slide ran through an election in which neither bloc reached 61 seats without Arab parties, leaving 19 Arab-party seats to decide who governs as Herzog opened coalition talks. Days earlier, Trump said $4 billion in Israel aid stops at year-end, and Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Democrats flipped 6 Senate seats and took the House in the midterms, and Vance said the Iran war was "the reason we lost". Two days later Stephen Miller replaced Wiles to run the White House from Monday, and Chutkan froze Trump's arch hours after it was approved.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: The Fed held in late October despite intensifying inflation, with TD Securities expecting 3 dissents, and markets now fully price a December hike. Employers then added 165,000 jobs in October against 65,000 forecast, and the midterms gave Democrats control of confirming every future Fed governor.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The ECB held rates on 29 October, the same day Christine Lagarde said she would leave on 7 February 2027. With eurozone inflation at 4%, Panetta and Nagel back a December hike, the third this year. Governments must now choose her successor: Klaas Knot, a hawk, or Pablo Hernández de Cos.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: October's report showed US employers added 165,000 jobs, well above the 65,000 forecast. Treasuries stumbled as traders raised their bets that the Fed hikes rates again, because a hiring pace that strong argues for tightening rather than for cuts.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.
xag.recent: Gold, the metal silver usually trades alongside, slid to a one-year low before dip buyers arrested the slide, then headed for its biggest weekly gain since August as the dollar and yields fell on the US midterm result. Nothing reported in the window speaks to silver's own mine supply or industrial demand.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: The Fed left interest rates unchanged in late October despite inflation running above where it wants it. Within days, higher oil and fresh US inflation data had traders betting on a Fed hike rather than a cut.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait is a war zone: Iran demands recognition of its sovereignty over it, the US struck Qeshm Island, tankers keep hitting mines, and UKMTO counted 11 attacks in the week to 4 Nov, with 3 ships sunk. A seafarer died aboard the Velos Sapphire; freight to Asia now costs $30-$35 a barrel, and India buys crude from about 43 countries.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal, at the other end of the same route, earned $724 million in October as traffic returned to the Red Sea. The Houthis spent the period firing missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia, hitting a refinery and a pipeline, declaring Riyadh airport a military target and attacking Aden, rather than at ships in the strait.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Egypt's Suez Canal doubled its revenue to $724 million in October. The Houthi missiles and drones of late October hit at Saudi Arabia itself, at oil sites, a pipeline and Riyadh's airport, rather than at shipping, so the canal held its traffic while Brent climbed.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from the far end of the tanker route: mines and attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and the USS Theodore Roosevelt calling at Singapore on its way to the Iran war. All of it postdates this series, so none of it explains Malacca's traffic.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's reporting was about mines and strikes on tankers around Hormuz, and all of it postdates the latest Gibraltar reading. None of it accounts for the fall in traffic here.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: A ceasefire the White House said Melania Trump secured let an aid convoy into besieged Oleshky and evacuees return. Ukraine, Russia and the US meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, their first US-mediated talks since February, with Rustem Umerov leading Kyiv's team; Brussels told Trump that Europe decides its own security.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: A backlash against data centres after the midterms hit chip makers hard: Nvidia fell 6% in one session, AMD 12% and Micron 11%. US officials have since told the Trump administration that Alice Huang, who is close to Jensen Huang, was a Chinese intelligence asset. The House Select Committee on China has asked him to a briefing.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Apple reported a record quarter carried by India, but its new CEO called memory prices "unprecedented" and guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, and about $140 billion came off its value after hours. In China, Siri now runs on Alibaba's Qwen, and the touchscreen M6 MacBook Pro launched from $1,999.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Alphabet's quarterly results showed capex up 114% to $51.4 billion, enough to turn its free cash flow negative, alongside a miss in search. They landed as tech earnings deepened a collapse in AI enthusiasm. A week later Google agreed to take over Anthropic's $19 billion TeraWulf data center lease if Anthropic defaults.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon's results showed its AI spending outrunning the cash the business brings in: over 12 months it burned a record $42.4 billion. The report landed in the same week other tech earnings deepened doubts about the AI trade, and investors marked down the companies paying for it.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to 60,000 employees to contain costs while forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year for its AI push. PC revenue slid, and Kaspersky found a bootkit, BlackX, infecting fully patched Windows machines past Secure Boot. None of it on its own accounts for the share's path.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.
co:broadcom.recent: The one report on Broadcom's own business in the fortnight was VMware's release of vSphere Express, virtualization software for machines of up to 128 cores. A product release of that size does not account for the fall in the share, and nothing else reported explains it.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: SpaceX borrowed $40 billion, mostly callable debt, to buy GPUs. In Ukraine, drones lost Starshield links above 160 km/h for 10 days, and the Pentagon inspector general then declined a nine-senator request to investigate. None of it accounts for the share price.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: Meta ended the quarter $2.12 billion cash-negative on AI spending and turned to outside money: a $95 billion stock sale, its largest ever, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyeing up to $5 billion of it, then an investment-grade bond sale. It also shelved terms claiming training rights over its customers' websites.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on the higher oil prices the Hormuz crisis brought, and the same day it began expanding an export route that bypasses Hormuz. Saudi Arabia will also store crude in Singapore's Jurong caverns from 2027, another way to keep barrels moving around the strait.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla is winding down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas after weak sales and multiple recalls; Cox Automotive estimates 11,586 were sold in nine months. Musk said the truck makes way for the Cybercab as the company turns to robotics and AI, and the shares rose on the news after a week caught in a tech-led selloff.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Its quarterly earnings rattled technology shares and dragged crypto down with them. The same week it stopped selling fridges and washing machines in Hong Kong, a retreat from appliances there. Days later it joined Tesla in opposing new US tariffs on Vietnam.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: About 12 Micron workers in Taoyuan staged Taiwan's first chip-industry strike, and Micron paused work on its $4.5 billion Taiwan plant after the labor spat. The same Thursday, chip stocks slid after the midterms: Micron fell 11%, alongside Nvidia and AMD.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD reported a record quarter in which data-center revenue jumped 97% to $8.55 billion while its gaming business cratered, and its sales forecast topped estimates on AI chip demand. Two days later the shares fell 12% as chip stocks slid after the midterms, alongside Nvidia and Micron.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: The one development in JPMorgan's own business was abroad: the CBN gave it approval-in-principle to set up a merchant bank in Nigeria, a first licensing step for a firm present in Lagos since 1961. Nothing in it accounts for the fall in the share.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: The one report on the company in the fortnight came on 2026-10-28, when SK Hynix lifted chip stocks and Nasdaq futures ahead of a Fed decision and its earnings. Nothing reported since accounts for the fall in its shares.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: The one thing Walmart did in the news was join Eli Lilly and 36 other issuers in objecting to tokenized versions of their shares on OKX-ICE. That dispute is about where its stock trades, not about how its stores sell, and nothing in the input accounts for the price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: The one report on ASML's own business pointed the other way: customers are already asking it for lithography tools to be delivered in 2029 and 2030. Nothing reported about the company in these weeks accounts for the fall.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.
ez-cpi.recent: October came in at 4%, the eighth straight month above 2%, and forecasters now expect the year to average 3.0%, which has opened a debate at the ECB over raising rates. Nothing in these reports says what is driving prices up.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The news from the network itself ran the other way: Schroders, a $1.1 trillion manager, put an emerging-market bond fund on Solana, and the network began charging 1 SOL per bug report after 809 reports, many of them AI spam, swamped its $1 million contest. Neither accounts for the slide.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: Ripple's final go-ahead for a U.S. national trust bank did nothing for the token, which then fell with the whole market: bitcoin dropped below $80,000, liquidating $356 million in longs, and a Binance hack sent bitcoin and ether tumbling. The XRP Ledger is also fixing a flaw that could let stablecoin partners print new tokens.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: Traders went offshore to Hyperliquid to bet at 10-fold leverage on Anthropic's initial public offering, a contract that showed what the venue lists beyond crypto. Nothing in the input accounts for the token's price over the window.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: Zcash's two biggest daily jumps came during wider crypto rallies: 8% on Oct 28 as Bitcoin neared $81,000 ahead of a Fed decision, and 12% on Nov 5 in a post-election rebound that held Bitcoin above $80,000. Neither headline names a cause specific to Zcash itself.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate a quarter point to 4%, its first hike since 2023, as the Iran war's energy shock pushed its inflation forecast to a 4.9% peak. Bailey said a second hike was more likely than not if the war goes on, while eurozone inflation reached 4% in October.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: The Bank of Japan held in late October, one of a G7 trio with the Fed and ECB pausing. Ueda said the 2% inflation goal was not yet sustainably achieved, a signal strategists said supported the yen, and on Nov 6 said he saw 'some upside risks' to inflation.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China left this rate untouched and fought on the currency instead. A record $938.1 billion trade surplus through September was pushing the yuan up, so it set a weaker fixing and raised the forex deposit reserve requirement, a step sized at up to $24 billion in foreign currency drawn out of the banks.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia raised its projected path for the key rate, warning that fourth-quarter inflation may reach 7.1-7.6%, and said the higher trajectory would bring inflation to 4% in 2027. Meanwhile it kept buying yuan in the domestic market, about $150 mln per settlement day.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: Thai consumer inflation hit 3.9%, above the Bank of Thailand's ceiling, driven by the energy and food costs the Iran war passed on through Brent crude. That leaves the central bank weighing a rate rise against households already cutting back, with Southeast Asians scaling down weddings under the energy crisis.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The trough came as the Houthis took the war onto Saudi soil. They claimed strikes on oil sites and a pipeline, air defences intercepted 10 ballistic missiles, and Riyadh airport stayed shut until flights resumed. The rebound followed the Saudi defence minister's talks in Tehran and Aramco's third-quarter profit of $31.2 billion, earned from the Hormuz crisis.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight's Gulf news ran through Hormuz. Oil from tankers attacked by Iran closed beaches in Ras Al Khaimah, Al Gharbia's pipe output fell from 250,000 to 60,000 tonnes, and by early November Gulf Arab producers were exporting crude at pre-war rates again. None of it is about the property developers and banks that make up Dubai's index.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Philippine businesses were described as fighting a weak peso and high inflation, Southeast Asians were scaling back weddings as an inflation and energy crisis took its toll, and Philippine bonds were ranked the most exposed in Emerging Asia to Fed hikes. None of it dates the slide itself.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: Meta ended the quarter $2.12 billion cash-negative on its AI spending, then turned to investors to pay for data centres: a $95 billion stock sale, its largest ever, which thins every existing holder's stake, followed by a cross-border investment-grade bond offering. Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom eyed up to $5 billion of the new stock.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: The rise dates from Tencent's preview of Hunyuan Hy4, and within a week the company said it had expanded Hy4 inference capacity tenfold to keep up with WorkBuddy demand. The day before the preview, QuestMobile counted 143 million monthly users on Lvpaopao, its short-drama service.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The fall bottomed out in Thursday's post-midterms sell-off, a backlash against data centres that hit AMD and Micron harder than Nvidia. Two days later, US officials were reported to believe Alice Huang, a woman close to Jensen Huang, was a Chinese intelligence asset, and the House Select Committee on China asked him to a briefing.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Houthi missiles and drones reached the kingdom's pipeline, its refineries and the Mecca region, and a claimed refinery strike lifted Brent. Riyadh answered with diplomacy and allies: its defence minister met Iran's president in Tehran, Egypt's parliament voted to defend Saudi Arabia, and Syrian military trainers arrived after a pact with Damascus.

poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the US, Russian and Chinese leaders meet together in person before 2027. A three-way meeting would put Beijing at the table on matters Washington and Moscow usually settle between themselves.
poly-trump-putin-and-xi-seen-together-be.recent: The fortnight's diplomacy ran between Russia and the US: Ukraine, Russia and the US meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, and Trump predicted a "very big" Russia deal covering all of Europe, which the EU rebuffed. None of it involved Xi or a meeting of all three, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-ex-cuba-leader-raul-castro-in-us-cu.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Raúl Castro, Fidel's brother, Cuba's president from 2008 to 2018 and party chief until 2021, is in US custody by year's end. Traders bet on Washington getting him before an American court.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: The parent company of Google, earning most of its revenue from search and YouTube advertising, alongside Google Cloud and Waymo. Its share is a running bet on whether AI assistants strengthen or erode the search ad business.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Search revenue missed on October 29 and Google conceded AI search makes less money, while capex jumped 114% to $51.4 billion in one quarter and free cash flow turned negative. Its own chips, built to challenge Nvidia, lifted cloud sales but deepened the cash burn; days later it agreed to backstop Anthropic's $19 billion data center lease.

poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis agree a ceasefire before the year ends. Its price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with strikes, mediation and the Red Sea shipping the war hangs over.
poly-saudi-houthi-ceasefire-agreement-an.recent: The fortnight brought escalation, not talks: the Saudi-led coalition says it shot down a Houthi drone near Mecca, Saudi strikes killed 17 civilians in Yemen, 281,000 Yemenis have been displaced since August, and Syrian military trainers are now inside Saudi Arabia. None of it accounts for the price.

poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether a US-Iran agreement reached in 2026 has Iran hand over its stockpile of enriched uranium, the material at the centre of the nuclear dispute and of any settlement between the two.
poly-will-a-us-iran-deal-in-2026-include.recent: Washington sent mixed signals: Trump answered "no" on striking Iran after the midterms, yet a third carrier strike group is one port call from the war. Tehran's five conditions demand recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz, and Mojtaba Khamenei says partisan shifts will not soften US hostility. None of it mentions handing over uranium.

poly-will-deepseek-ipo-by-december-31-20.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if DeepSeek, the Hangzhou AI lab spun out of the hedge fund High-Flyer, lists its shares before 2028. A listing would open China's most closely watched AI lab to public shareholders.

poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Venezuela's authorities formally schedule a national election before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on a vote being called, not on one being held.
poly-venezuela-election-scheduled-by-dec.recent: Venezuelans marched in Caracas on Thursday, 24 October, demanding that a presidential election date be set, and none followed. Nothing else carried in the fortnight concerns Venezuela, so nothing here explains the later shifts in the betting.

poly-will-any-country-join-the-mecca-agr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if any further country formally joins the Mecca Agreement before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the pact widening beyond its founding signatories.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Tinubu opened his re-election bid in Kaduna with petrol at about 1,400 naira a litre in September, the cost-of-living record Obi campaigns against. Tech firms also pledged help with the vote, and Microsoft said it would load Nigeria's candidate list into its AI systems. Neither story concerns Obi himself.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: The only truce agreed was local: a six-day ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump let civilians leave occupied Oleshky. The first US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks since February open in Abu Dhabi on 10 November with Europe left out, and the EU answered Trump's promise of a "very big" deal by saying "a lot of work" remains.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: The White House said Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire in Oleshky, but it was a six-day local truce that let civilians leave the occupied town, not a front-wide one. Ukraine, Russia and the US meet in Abu Dhabi on 10 November, the first US-mediated talks since February, and the EU rebuffed Trump's talk of a deal covering all of Europe.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple reported a record quarter carried by India, but its new CEO called memory prices "unprecedented" and guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, and the company lost about $140 billion in value after hours. The recovery came the next day, as Apple Intelligence began beta testing in China with Alibaba's Qwen running inside Siri.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Around the midterms the two sides talked past each other. Trump answered "no" on striking Iran again and said only he decides when the war ends. Tehran set five conditions, starting with recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz, and Mojtaba Khamenei said partisan shifts would not soften US hostility.

stocks:INTC.standing: The American chipmaker that both designs processors and makes them in its own fabs, the largest US bid at leading-edge manufacturing. Its share price answers to Washington's industrial policy as much as to PC and server demand.
stocks:INTC.recent: Intel reported quarterly revenue above its own guidance and still lost 23% after hours, because sales of its PC chips plunged while fears about AI spending were already pulling tech shares down. The fall took about $10 billion off the U.S. government's equity stake in the company.

stocks:BIDU.standing: Baidu runs China's dominant search engine and has staked its next chapter on artificial intelligence: its Ernie models, its cloud business and its Apollo Go robotaxis. Its US-listed shares trade on Nasdaq.
stocks:BIDU.recent: The fortnight brought Baidu product news, not results: in Shenzhen its Apollo unit showed Apollo World, a model that generates traffic reacting to the car so robotaxis can train on simulated scenarios, and in Wuhan its AI agent began turning residents' group chats into work orders. Neither accounts for the slide in the share.

stocks:BABA.standing: The New York-listed shares of China's largest e-commerce group, owner of Taobao and Tmall and the country's biggest cloud provider. The price carries Chinese consumer demand, Beijing's regulation and US-China tension.
stocks:BABA.recent: Apple chose Alibaba's Qwen to run its iPhone AI in China, putting the model behind Siri for Chinese users and handing Alibaba the largest foreign phone maker in the market as a customer. Days later Alibaba sold nearly 100,000 monthly AI passes at one fen each, pricing that trades revenue for users.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs one of China's largest short-video and livestreaming apps, the main rival to ByteDance's Douyin, and owns the Kling AI video generator. Advertising, livestream tips and e-commerce pay for it.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kling, Kuaishou's AI video unit, closed a record funding round of about 19.8 billion yuan, and the raise valued it above its parent, so a subsidiary is now priced at more than the platform that owns it. The round closed just after the late-October trough, and the shares recovered from there.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-november-30-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, goes public by the deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: The opposition's campaign against Kumar peaked without moving him. Kharge accused the commission of using voter-roll revisions to steal 4 state governments, and the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' march brought thousands to New Delhi demanding he resign. No step toward his removal followed the march.

poly-will-helen-zille-be-the-next-mayor-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Helen Zille, the former Cape Town mayor and Western Cape premier, becomes Johannesburg's next mayor. The city council elects the mayor, so coalition deals can matter as much as the vote.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: Trump answered "no" when asked about striking Iran after the midterms, and Vance said the Iran war was the reason Congress was lost. Tehran answered a US ceasefire proposal with five conditions, among them recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz. That kept the dispute at the negotiating table rather than pushing Iran toward leaving the NPT.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on bitcoin each day. Bitcoin is a digital currency with a capped supply and no central issuer, so price shocks, hacks and rule changes send newcomers to look it up.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Nothing in the input accounts for the early-October peak. Later, Chainalysis confirmed at least $5.9 billion stolen from Binance in a hack linked to North Korea, and users pulled a net $4.72 billion once withdrawals reopened. Bitcoin then fell below $75,000 as US bitcoin ETFs shed about $430 million in the AI-led tech rout.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: After the midterms, Trump answered "no" on striking Iran again, and Vance said Trump conceded the Iran war lost Congress. Trump also said only he decides when the war ends. Tehran answered with five conditions, including recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz, while a third US carrier strike group moved closer.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jon Ossoff, the Democratic senator from Georgia, becomes his party's presidential nominee in 2028. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.recent: The fortnight's news on prediction markets was about the venues rather than the race: the CFTC sued Utah over its ban on Kalshi, and Polymarket pledged $3.9 million back to victims after a site compromise. Nothing in it names Ossoff or explains why traders paid more for his nomination.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: After the Democratic sweep, Vance blamed the Iran war for losing Congress and Trump said only he decides when it ends. Tehran's five conditions include recognition of its sovereignty over Hormuz, Mojtaba Khamenei said the vote will not soften US hostility, and a third US carrier strike group is nearing; none of it says when the blockade lifts.
